patient.chief_complaint: Daughter found mother having continuous seizure for >20 minutes at home

past_medical_history: Ischemic stroke 3 years ago (right MCA territory, residual left arm weakness)

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Johnson is a 72-year-old retired teacher with post-stroke epilepsy on levetiracetam who is brought by ambulance after her daughter found her having a continuous seizure. The daughter arrived at her mother's home for a routine Sunday visit and found her on the living room floor in active convulsions. She estimated the seizure had been ongoing for at least 20 minutes based on the time she entered the home. She is not sure if her mother took her medications yesterday. The daughter reports her mother has been unwell for 3-4 days with a urinary tract infection treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole started 4 days ago, which she got from her primary care doctor via telephone. She has had poor oral intake and was possibly dehydrated. The patient has a known right MCA stroke territory residual with left arm weakness. On EMS arrival, continuous generalized tonic-clonic activity was present. Paramedics gave lorazepam 2 mg IV en route without termination. She arrived in active SE, now 25 minutes total. She is also on trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and metformin.
